observations: Photo 0 shows a collection of used car parts leaning against a wall.
One steering rack with hydraulic lines and tie rod ends is visible.
Two drive shafts (CV axles) with rubber boots are present.
One automotive radiator or condenser unit is standing on the right.
One starter motor is on the ground in the center.

claims.claim: Everything is clean, dry and sorted
claims.evidence: photo 0 shows visible dirt, grime, and rust on the parts.
The items shown (steering rack, two axles, radiator, starter) typically weigh between 35kg and 50kg total; 500kg is highly improbable for these specific items.

risks.risk: The actual weight is a fraction of the 500kg claimed, which affects scrap value.
risks.proof: A photo of all items together on a weighing scale.

risks.risk: The radiator/condenser may have leaks or internal blockages.
risks.proof: A video of a pressure test or a clear shot of the unit filled with fluid without leaking.

risks.risk: Mechanical parts (steering rack, starter) may be seized or internally damaged.
risks.proof: A video showing the steering rack moving freely and the starter motor being bench-tested.

proof_requests: A photo of the items on a scale to verify the 500kg weight claim.
Clearer photos of any manufacturer labels or part numbers on the steering rack and starter motor.
A video showing the condition of the drive shaft splines and the movement of the steering rack.
response.reason: No comparable price data for scrap car parts was provided. Additionally, the seller's claim of 500kg is physically inconsistent with the items pictured, which appear to weigh significantly less.
